questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Berlin?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Germany is Berlin.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Germany on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Germany on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Germany?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Germany on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Germany article.

questions.proof: The highest point is the Zugspitze on the Austrian border, at 2,962 metres (9,718 ft).

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Germany about 357,588 square kilometres; Czech Republic about 78,871 square kilometres; Denmark about 42,925 square kilometres; Netherlands about 37,378 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Germany?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Germany article.

questions.proof: During this time, the capital city of Berlin was divided into a west and an east part.
